text:
sasha: FYI saw a 15-25% token latency regression on the RLHF inference pool after we switched to the 'sandboxed' container profile that removes privileged mounts. nvprof/nsys traces attached show weird kernel thrash (multiple GEMM variants launching back-to-back). Not sure if it's kernel selection heuristic or KV-cache IO contention. Anyone seen this?
jordan: can you drop the nsys/nvprof output and a short perfetto timeline?
sasha: uploaded: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 and attached nsys: /artifacts/nsys_trace_1865551111.qdrep, nvprof: nvprof_out.txt. Main interesting bit: timeline shows repeated launches of cuBLASLtMatmul and cublasGemmEx variants for the same op across batches.
maya: quick q — did the sandbox change also modify how /tmp or /var is mounted? nvidia tooling writes to /tmp/.nv/ and if that fails, some drivers fall back or reinit different kernels.
sasha: yes — sandbox removes writable host /tmp mount and we don't have privileged mode. I checked inside container and /tmp/.nv is missing. ls -la /tmp shows root-owned dirs.
ryan: that's suspicious. nvtoolkit (and nsight) sometimes create sockets/files under /tmp to communicate with the driver. If creation fails, the runtime may pick a different codepath or reinitialize cublas handles per call -> extra syncs.
ben: also check ulimit for max open files and file descriptor leaks from the KV cache. Small batches + long context cause more concurrent kernels -> more file/socket ops. If those ops fail, fallback kernels might be used.
sasha: here's a minimal reproduce command we ran locally (k8s):
```
kubectl exec -it pod/rlhf-pod -- bash -c '\n  NV_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  python -u serve.py --batch-size 1 --seq-len 2048\n'
```
We profiled with nsys: `nsys profile --output ns_trace --trace=cuda,cudnn --stats true --sample=none --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx`
Got error-ish logs in nvprof_out.txt: `NVTOOLSEXTERR: Failed to open /tmp/.nv/nvtx.sock: Permission denied` and then we see alternate kernel launches.
ops-bot: note: cluster updated nvidia-container-toolkit to 1.12.0 during the sandbox rollout (see infra change #2345).
ci-bot: rolling back mount policy to previous privileged-enabled profile on one canary node scheduled (canary-3).
jordan: short checklist: 1) verify /tmp/.nv permissions inside sandboxed containers, 2) try chown/chmod on startup as pod init, 3) run nsys with full trace and `--capture-range=process` so we can correlate kernel timestamps, 4) check cublas heuristic env vars: `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` and any cuBLASLt tuning flags.
maya: temp workaround: add an initContainer that creates `/tmp/.nv` and chowns to the container uid. Example yaml snippet:
```
initContainers:
- name: nvtmp-fix
  image: busybox
  command: ['sh','-c','mkdir -p /tmp/.nv && chown 1000:1000 /tmp/.nv']
  securityContext:
    runAsUser: 0
```
try that on the canary.
ryan: also capture `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` to see which kernels are taking the longest and whether the same kernel variant shows higher launch latency. If it's repeated handle reinit, you'll see short gaps between launches.
ben: if it truly is kernel-selection oscillation, we can force a single preferred kernel via cuBLASLt heuristics or pin the heuristic mul algorithm in the model runtime as a mitigation while infra fixes the mounts.
sasha: plan: 1) apply initContainer fix to canary-3 (ci-bot already scheduling), 2) repro with nsys capture on canary, 3) if perf recovers -> add init step cluster-wide and open infra PR to revert the privileged mount removal, 4) if still broken, dig deeper into KV cache flush paths.
jordan: assigned eng-runtime perf ticket PERF-789 to investigate and collect traces.
sasha: thanks all — will post nsys qdrep + perfetto link once canary finishes. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: canary started at 1865551150, will report completion.
ops-bot: infra note: elevating this to infra-runtime oncall due to potential cluster-wide impact. :warning:
ryan: one last tip — when profiling inside k8s, mount host `/tmp` or pre-create `/tmp/.nv` in image to avoid intermittent permission-based fallbacks.
sasha: noted. collecting traces now. :thinking:
